title: Erdos #1160: Group Counting Maximized at Powers of 2

problemStatement.formal: Let g(n) be the number of non-isomorphic groups of order n. Is g(n) <= g(2^m) whenever n <= 2^m?
problemStatement.plain: Do powers of 2 always maximize the finite-group counting function among all group orders up to the same size bound?
whyMatters: Finite p-groups dominate the landscape of group enumeration, especially at powers of 2.
The conjecture asks for a pointwise dominance statement over an extremely irregular arithmetic function.
The Lean file turns the statement into equivalent formulations and verifies several small and structured cases.

proven: Lean axiomatizes the group-counting function numGroups and proves equivalent formulations of the main conjecture.
Derived values cover g(2), g(4), g(6), g(8), g(9), g(10), g(14), and g(15), with base-range proofs through m = 4.
The file proves useful transfer lemmas such as erdos_1160_lift and checks prime and small-power cases from the declared group-counting inputs.
open: numGroups is not computed from a Mathlib finite-group classification; it is an axiomatized interface.
Pantelidakis odd-order and asymptotic growth statements are present as propositions or context, not Lean-proved theorems.
knownResults.goal: Record the precise group-counting conjecture and verified small cases while making the ten active axioms visible.

currentState.focus: Metadata now fills the missing problem statement and distinguishes proved small-case consequences from the axiomatized group-counting table and structural inputs.
blockers: The full maximization conjecture is open.
currentState.nextAction: Future work should either replace small group-counting axioms with formal classifications or extend verified finite ranges beyond m = 4.

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEYED: 10 axioms confirmed deep (group classification). No further elimination possible. File complete for m≤4. Extending to m=5 needs 6 new value axioms.
